Definition / Formula: Daily portfolio std. dev. of returns x sqrt(252)
Interpretation: Measures how much the portfolio value fluctuates over a year. <15% = Low, 15-25% = Moderate, 25-35% = High, >35% = Very High (typical Indian equity ranges).

Definition / Formula: 5th percentile of the actual 252-day daily P&L distribution, ranked worst to best
Interpretation: On 95 of 100 trading days, the loss is expected to stay within this amount. Uses real historical scenarios, no distributional assumption.

Definition / Formula: 1st percentile of the 252-day daily P&L distribution
Interpretation: A more extreme loss threshold than 95% VaR. Expected to be breached only ~2-3 times a year under normal conditions.

Definition / Formula: z(1.645) x portfolio daily volatility x portfolio value
Interpretation: Fast to compute but assumes returns are normally distributed, so it tends to underestimate tail risk in real (fat-tailed) markets.

Definition / Formula: z(2.326) x portfolio daily volatility x portfolio value
Interpretation: Same normality assumption as 95% parametric VaR but for a more extreme confidence level.

Definition / Formula: 5th percentile of 10,000 simulated correlated daily P&L scenarios (Cholesky decomposition of covariance matrix)
Interpretation: Most robust VaR method here since it directly captures cross-asset correlation effects rather than assuming a single distribution.

Definition / Formula: Mean of all historical daily P&L scenarios that fall below the VaR 95% threshold
Interpretation: Answers 'if losses exceed VaR, how bad on average?'. Captures tail severity that VaR alone ignores.

Definition / Formula: VaR 99% divided by VaR 95%
Interpretation: Near 1.0 = thin-tailed/near-normal distribution. Above ~1.5 = fat tails, i.e. extreme losses disproportionately larger than moderate ones.

Definition / Formula: Historical VaR 95% / CVaR 95%
Interpretation: Always <=1. Close to 1 means losses rarely exceed VaR by much (thin tail). Well below 1 = tail losses can be much worse than VaR (warning sign).

Definition / Formula: (Parametric VaR 95% - Historical VaR 95%) / Historical VaR 95%, in %
Interpretation: Positive = parametric model is conservative (overestimates risk). Negative = parametric underestimates risk (dangerous). Large divergence signals non-normal returns.

Definition / Formula: Euler decomposition: weight_i x marginal VaR_i x portfolio value, summed = total Parametric VaR
Interpretation: Attributes total portfolio VaR to each holding. Negative component VaR = that stock provides a diversification benefit, reducing overall risk.

Definition / Formula: d(Portfolio VaR) / d(weight of holding i)
Interpretation: Sensitivity of portfolio risk to a small increase in a position's weight. High marginal VaR = that stock is a key risk driver; adding more raises risk disproportionately.

Definition / Formula: Market value of holding / total portfolio value
Interpretation: Share of capital allocated to a position. Negative weight implies a net short position (cumulative sold > bought in the tradebook).

Definition / Formula: Bucketing current annualised volatility into Low / Moderate / High / Very High
Interpretation: Quick qualitative read on whether the portfolio is currently in a calm or turbulent risk regime.

Definition / Formula: Simple average of Historical VaR 95% over the trailing 6 monthly snapshots
Interpretation: Baseline to judge whether current risk is elevated or subdued relative to the recent trend.

Definition / Formula: Cov(portfolio returns, benchmark returns) / Var(benchmark returns)
Interpretation: Systematic risk relative to the market. Beta > 1 = more volatile than benchmark; < 1 = less volatile; negative = moves opposite to the benchmark.

Definition / Formula: sqrt( mean( min(0, R_i - MAR)^2 ) ), annualised
Interpretation: Volatility computed using only returns below a Minimum Acceptable Return (MAR). Unlike std. dev., it ignores upside variability, which investors don't mind.

Definition / Formula: Third standardised moment of the return distribution
Interpretation: Negative skew = frequent small gains with occasional large losses (typical of equity strategies); positive skew = frequent small losses, occasional large gains.

Definition / Formula: Fourth standardised moment of the return distribution, minus 3
Interpretation: Excess kurtosis > 0 = fat tails / more extreme outliers than a normal distribution, i.e. higher chance of large surprise moves.

Definition / Formula: Annualised std. dev. of (portfolio return - benchmark return)
Interpretation: How much the portfolio's returns deviate from its benchmark. Higher tracking error = more active/concentrated bets away from the benchmark.

Definition / Formula: Square of the correlation coefficient between portfolio and benchmark returns
Interpretation: Proportion of portfolio return variance explained by the benchmark. High R^2 = portfolio moves closely with benchmark; low R^2 = returns driven by idiosyncratic/stock-specific factors.

Definition / Formula: Pearson correlation of daily returns between each pair of holdings
Interpretation: High positive correlations across holdings reduce diversification benefit; negative/low correlations improve it.

Definition / Formula: Sum of squared position weights across all holdings
Interpretation: Higher HHI = more concentrated portfolio (fewer effective bets), higher idiosyncratic risk; lower HHI = more diversified.

Definition / Formula: (NAV_t / NAV_(t-1)) - 1
Interpretation: Simple percentage change in portfolio value from one period to the next; building block for all other return metrics.

Definition / Formula: (NAV_end / NAV_start) - 1
Interpretation: Overall percentage gain or loss over the full period, ignoring the path taken to get there.

Definition / Formula: (NAV_end / NAV_start)^(365/days) - 1
Interpretation: The constant annual growth rate that would produce the same total return; the standard way to compare performance across different time horizons.

Definition / Formula: Average of periodic returns (simple mean)
Interpretation: Simple average return per period; overstates true compounded growth when returns are volatile.

Definition / Formula: [Product(1+R_i)]^(1/n) - 1
Interpretation: Return accounting for compounding; the mathematically correct average for comparing growth over multiple periods.

Definition / Formula: (Annualised Return - Risk-Free Rate) / Annualised Volatility
Interpretation: Excess return earned per unit of total risk (volatility). Higher is better; >1 is generally considered good, >2 very good.

Definition / Formula: (Annualised Return - MAR) / Downside Deviation
Interpretation: Like Sharpe but penalises only downside volatility. Preferred when upside volatility shouldn't count against the strategy.

Definition / Formula: Annualised Return / |Maximum Drawdown|
Interpretation: Return earned per unit of worst-case peak-to-trough loss. Popular for strategies where large drawdowns are the key risk to avoid.

Definition / Formula: Annualised Return / (Average of the largest N drawdowns + adjustment, typically 10%)
Interpretation: Similar intent to Calmar but uses an average of significant drawdowns instead of just the single worst one, reducing sensitivity to one outlier event.

Definition / Formula: (Annualised Return - Risk-Free Rate) / Beta
Interpretation: Excess return per unit of systematic (market) risk. Useful for well-diversified portfolios where idiosyncratic risk has largely been diversified away.

Definition / Formula: Portfolio Return - [Risk-Free Rate + Beta x (Benchmark Return - Risk-Free Rate)]
Interpretation: Return earned in excess of what CAPM predicts given the portfolio's beta. Positive alpha = manager added value beyond market exposure.

Definition / Formula: (Portfolio Return - Benchmark Return) / Tracking Error
Interpretation: Consistency of outperformance versus the benchmark, risk-adjusted for how much the portfolio deviates from it. Higher = more reliable alpha generation.

Definition / Formula: Sum of returns above a threshold / |Sum of returns below the threshold| (probability-weighted)
Interpretation: Captures the full shape of the return distribution (all moments), not just mean/variance. >1 means gains outweigh losses relative to the threshold.

Definition / Formula: Number of positive-return periods / Total number of periods
Interpretation: Fraction of days/months the strategy was profitable. High win rate alone doesn't guarantee profitability if losses are large.

Definition / Formula: Mean return of winning periods; Mean return of losing periods
Interpretation: Shows typical size of gains vs losses. Combined with win rate, indicates whether the edge comes from frequency or magnitude.

Definition / Formula: Sum of all gains / |Sum of all losses|
Interpretation: Ratio of total profit to total loss. >1 means the strategy is net profitable; higher values indicate a stronger edge.

Definition / Formula: Sum of monthly returns / |Sum of negative monthly returns|
Interpretation: Similar to profit factor but computed on monthly data; commonly used to judge smoothness of returns for allocators.

Definition / Formula: Return computed over a moving window, recalculated at each date
Interpretation: Shows consistency of performance across different starting points, revealing whether returns depend heavily on the specific entry date chosen.

Definition / Formula: Portfolio Return - Benchmark Return (e.g. Nifty 50) over the same period
Interpretation: Direct measure of active outperformance or underperformance versus the chosen benchmark.

Definition / Formula: (NAV_t - Running Peak NAV up to t) / Running Peak NAV
Interpretation: Percentage decline from the most recent all-time high. Always <= 0; 0 means the portfolio is at a new peak.

Definition / Formula: Minimum value of the drawdown series over the full history
Interpretation: The single worst peak-to-trough loss ever experienced. Key measure of worst-case historical pain; used in Calmar/Sterling ratios.

Definition / Formula: Mean of all negative drawdown values over the period (or mean of trough values of each distinct drawdown episode)
Interpretation: Typical magnitude of declines experienced, giving a sense of 'normal' pain versus the worst-case MDD.

Definition / Formula: Number of days/periods from a peak to the point the drawdown reaches its trough
Interpretation: How long it takes to hit bottom once a decline begins; longer duration can be harder for investors to tolerate psychologically.

Definition / Formula: Number of days/periods from the trough back to a new all-time high (previous peak)
Interpretation: Measures resilience - how quickly the strategy recoups losses. Longer recovery time means capital is 'stuck' underwater for longer.

Definition / Formula: Total number of days/periods the NAV is below its previous peak
Interpretation: Cumulative time spent in any drawdown, not just the worst one. High TuW indicates the strategy spends much of its life recovering rather than compounding.

Definition / Formula: sqrt( mean( Drawdown_t^2 ) ) over the period
Interpretation: Root-mean-square of drawdowns, penalising both depth and duration of declines. Higher ulcer index = more sustained/severe pain (the 'stress' the investor feels).

Definition / Formula: Mean of |Drawdown_t| over the period
Interpretation: Average magnitude of drawdown across all periods (not just when in a drawdown). Similar intent to Ulcer Index but linear rather than squared.

Definition / Formula: Annualised Return / Pain Index
Interpretation: Return earned per unit of average drawdown pain endured, analogous to Calmar but using Pain Index instead of Maximum Drawdown.

Definition / Formula: Sum of the 'underwater' area (drawdown depth x duration) / Sum of the NAV curve area
Interpretation: Visualises drawdowns as a 'lake' below the high-water-mark line; higher ratio = more of the equity curve's life spent underwater.

Definition / Formula: (Latest NAV - Running Peak NAV) / Running Peak NAV, as of the report date
Interpretation: How far the portfolio currently sits below its most recent all-time high; tells you if you're presently 'in the hole'.

Definition / Formula: Count of distinct peak-to-trough-to-recovery cycles exceeding a minimum depth threshold
Interpretation: Frequency of meaningful declines; useful alongside average depth/duration to characterise drawdown behaviour.

Definition / Formula: Average of the worst X% of drawdowns over the historical period
Interpretation: Tail-risk analogue of CVaR but applied to the drawdown series rather than single-period returns; captures clustering of bad periods.

Definition / Formula: Total portfolio market value (or per-unit value) at each date, indexed/normalised to a base (e.g. 100 or 1)
Interpretation: The core equity curve; all return, risk, and drawdown metrics are derived from its time series.

Definition / Formula: Running maximum of the NAV series up to time t
Interpretation: The peak value the portfolio has ever reached. Used as the reference point for computing drawdowns and (in funds) for performance-fee calculations.

Definition / Formula: Running product of (1+R_i) - 1, plotted over time
Interpretation: Visual growth-of-₹1 (or ₹100) chart showing compounding effect over the full history.

Definition / Formula: Annualised std. dev. of returns computed over a moving window (e.g. 30/60/90-day)
Interpretation: Shows how risk has evolved over time rather than a single static number; spikes indicate periods of market stress.

Definition / Formula: Sharpe ratio recomputed over a moving window
Interpretation: Tracks whether risk-adjusted performance is improving, stable, or deteriorating through time.

Definition / Formula: Plot of Drawdown_t (NAV vs running HWM) across the full history
Interpretation: Visual complement to the NAV curve, highlighting depth and duration of every drawdown episode at a glance.

Definition / Formula: (NAV_end / NAV_start)^(365/days) - 1
Interpretation: Same as CAGR but computed directly from the indexed NAV series; the headline long-run growth rate of the equity curve.

Definition / Formula: Max / Min of the periodic return series (day, month, or year)
Interpretation: Extremes of the return distribution realised historically; useful sanity check alongside VaR/CVaR.

Definition / Formula: Count of periods where return > 0 vs return < 0
Interpretation: Simple consistency check on the NAV curve's day-to-day or month-to-month behaviour, feeding into Win Rate.

Definition / Formula: Sum of market value of all holdings in a sector / Total portfolio value
Interpretation: Shows how capital is spread across sectors (e.g. Financials, IT, Energy). Heavy tilt to one sector raises exposure to sector-specific shocks (e.g. rate-sensitive financials, IT demand cycles).

Definition / Formula: Sum of market value of all holdings in an industry (sub-sector) / Total portfolio value
Interpretation: Finer-grained than sector allocation (e.g. 'Private Banks' vs all 'Financials'); reveals concentration a sector-level view can mask.

Definition / Formula: Portfolio sector weight - Benchmark (e.g. Nifty 50) sector weight
Interpretation: Positive = overweight that sector vs the benchmark, negative = underweight. Shows where the active bets relative to the index actually are.

Definition / Formula: Market value of a single stock / Total portfolio value
Interpretation: Position-level concentration. Position size limits (e.g. no single stock >5-10%) are a standard risk control.

Definition / Formula: Sum of weights of the N largest positions by market value
Interpretation: High top-N concentration means portfolio performance is dominated by a handful of names; low concentration implies broader diversification.

Definition / Formula: Count of distinct positions with non-zero net quantity
Interpretation: Simple headline diversification measure; more holdings generally (but not always) means less idiosyncratic risk per name.

Definition / Formula: 1 / HHI, where HHI = sum of squared position weights
Interpretation: Diversification measured in 'equivalent equal-weight positions'. E.g. Effective N = 12 with 40 actual holdings means concentration is really equivalent to just 12 equal bets.

Definition / Formula: Sum of (position weight)^2 across all holdings
Interpretation: Ranges from ~0 (fully diversified) to 1 (single stock). Higher HHI = more concentrated, higher stock-specific (idiosyncratic) risk.

Definition / Formula: Sum of (sector weight)^2 across all sectors
Interpretation: Same idea as stock-level HHI but applied to sector weights; flags sector concentration risk even if individual stock weights look fine.

Definition / Formula: Weighted average of individual holding volatilities / Portfolio volatility
Interpretation: Ratio > 1 shows the benefit of diversification - the portfolio is less volatile than the weighted average of its parts. Higher ratio = more diversification benefit captured.

Definition / Formula: Mean of the off-diagonal entries of the holdings' return correlation matrix
Interpretation: Low/negative average correlation = holdings tend to move independently (good diversification); high average correlation = holdings move together, reducing the diversification benefit of adding more names.

Definition / Formula: Sum of market value of holdings in each cap bucket / Total portfolio value
Interpretation: Shows style/size tilt. Small/mid-cap heavy portfolios usually carry higher volatility and liquidity risk than large-cap heavy ones.

Definition / Formula: (Sum of |long position values| + |short position values|) / Portfolio value
Interpretation: Total market exposure including leverage from shorts. Gross exposure > 100% implies use of leverage.

Definition / Formula: (Sum of long position values - Sum of short position values) / Portfolio value
Interpretation: Directional market exposure. Net exposure near 100% = fully long-biased; near 0% = market-neutral; negative = net short.

Definition / Formula: Sum of long position weights vs sum of |short position weights|
Interpretation: Shows how much of the book is long vs short; relevant for long-short or market-neutral strategies.

Definition / Formula: (Portfolio value - Sum of invested position values) / Portfolio value
Interpretation: Uninvested cash buffer. High cash weight lowers market exposure and can be a drag in rising markets but a cushion in falling ones.

Definition / Formula: Min(Total buys, Total sells) over a period / Average portfolio value over that period
Interpretation: How frequently holdings are traded/replaced. High turnover raises transaction costs and taxes; low turnover suggests a buy-and-hold style.

Definition / Formula: 0.5 x Sum of |portfolio weight_i - benchmark weight_i| across all stocks (portfolio + benchmark union)
Interpretation: Percentage of the portfolio that differs from the benchmark. High active share = truly active management; low active share = portfolio closely hugs the benchmark ('closet indexing').

Definition / Formula: Sum over holdings of [position value / (ADV x participation rate)], weighted by position size
Interpretation: Estimates how long it would take to exit the portfolio without excessive market impact. Higher values flag potential liquidity risk in stress scenarios.
